raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

`FSDPCheckpointManager.load_checkpoint` loads a LoRA-only checkpoint with `strict=False` (it legitimately lacks the frozen base weights) and already raises on unexpected keys, but never looks at `missing_keys`. If the checkpoint lacks some adapter tensors (e.g. a different `target_modules`, or a truncated/partial save), those tensors silently keep their fresh initialization while the rest of the adapter and the optimizer state are restored, and training resumes from a model that is neither the saved one nor a clean start.

This PR raises a `ValueError` when any missing key is a LoRA/adapter key (same `lora_` / `.adapter_` rule as `is_lora_only_state_dict`). Missing base weights are still accepted.

Scope: the check runs per rank after that rank's `load_state_dict`. Every rank saves the same key set, so a checkpoint that lacks adapter keys (e.g. a different adapter config) fails on every rank. A shard corrupted on only one rank is not handled here: with FSDP1 the ranks may already diverge inside the sharded load, and otherwise only that rank raises. Catching that would need a preflight of expected adapter names plus a collective failure flag, which is left out to keep this change small.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=lora+only+checkpoint+missing+keys (no existing fix)
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

New test `test_load_lora_only_checkpoint_missing_adapter_key_raises` in `tests/checkpoint_engine/test_fsdp_lora_only_checkpoint_on_cpu.py`: saves a LoRA-only checkpoint, drops the `lora_B` tensors from it, and loads it into a fresh model. The test fake's `load_state_dict` now reports real `missing_keys` (it always returned `[]` before); the existing tests are unchanged and still pass.

```
upstream main + new test:  1 failed, 16 passed   (Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError)
this PR:                   17 passed
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/checkpoint/fsdp_checkpoint_manager.py`: check `result.missing_keys` for adapter keys after the LoRA-only load.
- Test fake reports missing keys; one new test.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks (ruff 0.12.2 check / format on the changed files).
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation. (Not needed.)
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to the CI workflow (`*_on_cpu.py`, picked up by the CPU unit tests).

+    def test_load_lora_only_checkpoint_missing_adapter_key_raises(self, tmp_path):
+        import torch
+
+        mgr = self._make_fsdp_manager(
+            checkpoint_config={"save_lora_only": True, "save_contents": ["model"]},
+            model=_FakeFSDPModel(has_lora=True),
+        )
+        save_dir = tmp_path / "lora_only"
+        mgr.save_checkpoint(local_path=str(save_dir), global_step=1)
+        saved_path = save_dir / "model_world_size_1_rank_0.pt"
+        state_dict = torch.load(saved_path, weights_only=False)
+        state_dict = {k: v for k, v in state_dict.items() if "lora_B" not in k}
+        torch.save(state_dict, saved_path)
+
+        model_after = _FakeFSDPModel(has_lora=True)
+        model_after._fsdp_wrapped_module.lora_B_weight.data.fill_(7.0)
+        mgr2 = self._make_fsdp_manager(checkpoint_config={"load_contents": ["model"]}, model=model_after)
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="missing adapter keys"):
+            mgr2.load_checkpoint(local_path=str(save_dir))
+
     def test_load_full_checkpoint_still_works(self, tmp_path):
         model = _FakeFSDPModel(has_lora=True)
         model._fsdp_wrapped_module.base_weight.data.fill_(42.0)
